title: Groundbreaking Transplant Restores Woman's Sight
paragraphs: A woman in Italy who had been blind for five years has been able to see again after undergoing what doctors have described as the world's first macula transplant.

The operation was carried out by Dr. Michele Reibaldi and his team at Molinette Hospital in Turin, which announced the result on July 27, 2026. The patient, a 67-year-old woman named Elena, had lost her sight in a serious road accident.

The accident had damaged the optic nerve of Elena's left eye, which carries signals from the eye to the brain. As a result, the eye could no longer send images to the brain, even though the eye itself remained structurally intact. Meanwhile, her right eye had been so badly damaged that both the retina and the cornea, the clear front surface of the eye, could not be repaired. A standard cornea transplant was not possible, because the part of the eye containing important stem cells had also been damaged.

To solve this problem, the surgeons came up with an unusual solution. They took healthy tissue from the left eye, which could no longer be used for seeing, and transplanted it into the right eye. This included the cornea and the macula, which is the central part of the retina and is responsible for seeing fine details. In effect, the doctors used parts of two damaged eyes to create one working eye. The operation took almost six hours, and the hospital described it as a "biological transplant."

According to the hospital, Elena's sight has been restored. However, Reibaldi explained that it is still too early to know how well the transplanted retina will work in the long term. He described the first results as encouraging.
It should be noted that the information comes from the hospital's announcement, and the results have not yet been confirmed independently or published in a scientific journal.
